learning: Check s-bend and slalom max_error and progress against iteration 4 (0.062, 0.127 and 0.093). If s-bend progress falls below 0.127 or oval oscillation exceeds 0.25, the turn gain is overshooting, so return to a 0.10 m track. If oval oscillation exceeds 0.25 with max_error unchanged, move sensor y to 0.03. Report per-track values.
notes: Applies the Builder's narrow-track, light-mass contingency on the validated sensor array. Controller is unchanged from iteration 4 so the race isolates the geometry change.
rationale: Iteration 4 (wheel_track 0.10, body_length 0.12, mass 0.7, validated ±0.08 m, 0.04 m spacing, 0.016 m footprint array) kept line loss at zero on all tracks and held rms_error near 0.02. Oval finish rate was 65% and oval steering_oscillation 0.174, both within target. The s-bend and slalom still ended off_track at max_error about 0.062 with progress 0.127 and 0.093, so turn response is still the limit. I apply the Builder's requested contingency: wheel_track 0.09 m and mass 0.6 kg. The sensor array, sensor y 0.05, body 0.12 x 0.12 m and wheel radius 0.03 m are unchanged, so sensing is not varied. Narrowing the track raises turn gain per PWM count by about 1.11x, and the lower mass reduces yaw inertia, so I keep kp 6, ki 0.05, kd 0.9 and base_speed 1.5 to isolate the geometry change. The main risk is overshoot: s-bend progress fell from 0.177 to 0.127 when the track narrowed earlier, so if progress falls again or oval oscillation rises above 0.25, the next step should return to a 0.10 m track. Expected result: s-bend and slalom max_error below 0.06 m with progress above 0.13, and oval finish rate at or above 55%.
